transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-11-11
Time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~62 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Samir Patel (Redwood SE), Iris Gomez (Redwood CSM); Jordan Lee (Arcadia CTO), Priya Nair (Lead ML Eng), Tom Ruiz (SRE)

Auto-summary: Quick scoping for benchmark harness integration. Focus on making Arcadia's scripts run in Redwood's harness, defining success: throughput buckets, p99 tail, failure tolerances, streaming fallback behavior, warmup/kvcache expectations, and a realistic timeline for a two-week acceptance window.

--- Transcript (timestamps approximate) ---
[00:00] Maya (AE): Alright everyone thanks for joining, quick intro then we'll get into the stic— the script handoff and SLOs. Jordan, Priya, Tom, can you confirm audio?
[00:12] Jordan (CTO): Yep, loud and clear. Thanks, Maya.
[00:16] Samir (SE): Cool, I'll jump into the adapter details later, but first can you tell us what you mean by "customer script" in your workflow? Full end-to-end? pre- and post-processing?
[00:25] Priya (Lead ML Eng): Yeah it's the whole shebang — prompt building, a retry wrapper, some local caching for session state, and we do token-level post-filtering for PII. Mostly python.
[00:36] Maya: Perfect, that maps well. Our harness accepts a small adapter shim, we call it the harness-adapter, that wraps your script and handles streaming vs chunked cases. We'll send the template.
[00:48] Tom (SRE): Quick Q — does the harness expect requests to be idempotent? We have some side-effecting calls in our pre-hook.
[00:55] Samir: Good question. Ideally the adapter should isolate side-effects; for load runs we recommend a dry-run mode or mocking those external calls. The harness can also emit per-request metadata so you can correlate, but side-effects during a synthetic run will skew results.
[01:12] Jordan: Makes sense. On success criteria — we want <= 150ms median, p95 under 400ms, p99 under 900ms for 90% of the traffic slice. Is that realistic?
[01:26] Samir: It's tight depending on model size and streaming. For a 13B model with quantization and prefix cache warmed, median 150ms is plausible, but tail will depend on cold starts and concurrency. We should define the traffic slice.
[01:40] Priya: We'll provide a 10% representative slice — shorter prompts, interactive chat patterns. Also we'll include a longer 2–3% tail with 1k+ token sequences for stress.
[01:52] Maya: Good. We'll capture token length distribution and report SLO windows. Also want to call out K V cache behavior — our prefix cache drastically reduces repeated prefix cost, but the harness needs to populate warmup keys.
[02:07] Tom: How do you handle KV warmup on streaming? We sometimes see big spikes at warmup windows.
[02:14] Samir: For streaming, warmup is trickier. We have two modes: continuous warmup where we replay representative traces so the KV gets populated, or staged warmup where the first N requests in a window are treated specially. For acceptance you can run a warmup ramp for 10–20 minutes before measuring.
[02:33] Priya: That ramp time — do you account for it in the report? We need raw numbers excluding warmup as well as system-stable numbers.
[02:41] Maya: Yes, baseline and stable windows. Baseline for raw cold-starts; stable for steady-state SLOs.
[02:48] Jordan: We're concerned about streaming fallbacks — if streaming stalls do you switch to non-streaming automatically? We can't accept large partial responses.
[02:56] Samir: We support fallback policies: automatic fallback from stream to chunked non-streaming, or an immediate error depending on your policy. We can set thresholds like 'if client ack latency > X then fallback'. We'll share example policies.
[03:12] Tom: Any differences in harness metrics for streaming? We need per-chunk latencies and end-to-end deliver times.
[03:20] Samir: Yup, harness emits per-chunk timing, first-byte/last-byte, plus callback ACKs. It's a lot of telemetry; we can push to your S3 or cloud storage.
[03:30] Priya: About determinism — our scoring pipeline needs consistent outputs during regression checks. Does the harness pin RNG seeds or quantization jitters?
[03:38] Samir: We can pin seeds and use deterministic kernels for the test runs. Quantization introduces small differences but we log similarity metrics and embed a delta threshold.
[03:47] Maya: Let's talk timeline: we propose a 2-week window. Week 0: adapter onboarding + smoke; Week 1: baseline non-streaming runs + analysis; Week 2: streaming acceptance and fallbacks. Does that fit your release calendar?
[04:02] Jordan: That aligns, though we might need an extra day for internal sign-off.
[04:07] Maya: Fine. We'll pad a couple days.
[04:10] (--- quick micro break, 03:50 mins in ---)
[04:15] Priya: On harness infra, do we need to provide keys or tokens? We prefer not to put prod data in the run.
[04:22] Iris (CSM): We recommend obfuscated or synthetic data. For any secrets we support short-lived tokens and you can run in a VPC/hybrid.
[04:31] Tom: VPC — can the harness talk back to our private endpoints?
[04:35] Samir: For Private customers yes. For hosted benchmarks we proxy via a secure tunnel or you can bring a private instance. We'll note options in the adapter README.
[04:47] Jordan: Competitor note — we trialed ModelServeX last year; their streaming chops were okay but they fell over on long token sequences. Hoping this is better.
[04:58] Maya: We'll make sure to include long-tail stress tests.
[05:03] Priya: For the scripts themselves, we have a retry wrapper that does exponential backoff. How will that interact with harness concurrency?
[05:12] Samir: Retries need to be controlled at the adapter layer, otherwise you double-count requests. The adapter should surface a retry policy that the harness can respect. We'll add a sample.
[05:22] Tom: Anything special about batch vs streaming with your runtime? Our traffic is a mixture.
[05:27] Samir: Streaming favors low-latency interactive flows; batch is efficient for throughput and cold-batch inference. The harness supports mixed-mode runs, you can tag traffic and we'll run a blended profile. Important to report per-mode unit economics.
[05:43] Jordan: On metrics we need cost-per-1k-tokens estimates too, during the benchmark.
[05:48] Maya: We'll include cost proxies and a token accounting CSV.
[05:52] Priya: Can we run an initial non-streaming baseline at lower QPS to validate correctness before load spike?
[05:59] Samir: Absolutely — smoke tests at 1-2 qps, then ramp. We'll provide ramp templates.
[06:06] (--- timestamps skip forward, mid-session notes, some cross-talk) ---
[25:10] Samir: ...so sample adapter code — you'll see an ENV var to toggle streaming true/false, and a handler that yields chunks. We recommend architecting the script so chunk emission is a single generator.
[25:25] Priya: That will be fine. We'll need to refactor one of our legacy handlers which currently writes to disk mid-request.
[25:33] Tom: Disk writes — not great during high-concurrency. We'll mock those out.
[25:40] Maya: For SLO synthesis, can we agree on acceptance gates? I propose: 1) Baseline correctness pass (100% success on 200 sample requests), 2) Stable window SLOs: median/p95/p99 thresholds, 3) No more than 0.5% request failures due to harness errors, 4) Streaming fallback success for any degraded stream under policy.
[25:58] Jordan: Agree with those gates, though 0.5% might be tight — maybe 1% tolerated?
[26:06] Priya: Can we define what counts as a harness error vs model error? We need clarity for RCA.
[26:13] Samir: We'll tag errors. Harness errors are transport/adapter/runtime errors. Model errors are generation anomalies. We'll attach logs and correlation IDs for RCA.
[26:25] Tom: We'll need the raw traces for 100 failing requests for analysis.
[26:29] Maya: Noted.
[26:33] (--- later: deep-dive on telemetry schema ---)
[39:20] Samir: Telemetry payload includes request_id, start_ts, first_byte_ts, last_byte_ts, model_variant, quantization_flag, kv_hit_ratio, chunks_emitted, client_ack_latency. We'll provide schema and a sample parquet.
[39:36] Priya: kv_hit_ratio — how is that computed?
[39:39] Samir: It's the fraction of predicted prefix keys that were served from cache vs recomputed. Rough proxy but helpful.
[39:49] Jordan: For the long-tail test, what's the recommended load shape? We want sustained 200 qps with 5% spikes to 1k for 30s.
[39:58] Samir: We can model that. We'll also run staircase ramps and a randomized burst run.
[40:05] Tom: How do you capture cold starts for those spikes? We need to ensure cold v warm buckets are separated.
[40:11] Maya: The harness will label warmup windows; we'll exclude warmup when reporting steady state but include cold-start stats in a separate table.
[40:20] Priya: Any concerns with our post-filtering step (PII removal) adding variable latency?
[40:26] Samir: Post-filtering running in the adapter will add variance. Best to run a stripped-down version for perf tests, and a functional run for correctness. We'll keep both.
[40:36] (--- planning the actual handoff ---)
[50:05] Maya: Action checklist: we'll upload adapter template to the shared drive, Samir will upload the telemetry schema and ramp templates, Priya will produce two converted scripts, Tom will push traffic slice. We'll reconvene after scripts uploaded.
[50:19] Priya: One ask — can we redact session ids in logs before you ingest?
[50:24] Iris: Yes, we can accept redacted logs; if you want full logs we recommend a private tunnel.
[50:31] Jordan: Last Q: If streaming fails and fallback to chunked happens, how do you preserve ordering and session affinity?
[50:40] Samir: The adapter maintains session ids and sequence numbers; fallback is seamless from a session perspective if you choose the 'adhesive fallback' policy. We'll include that in the README.
[50:53] Maya: Great. Any blockers on timeline?
[50:56] Jordan: None now. We'll aim to have scripts by 11/18.
[51:02] Maya: Perfect. We'll send the deck and templates within 24 hours.
[51:06] (meeting close, quick recap)
[61:30] Maya: Recap: share adapter template, telemetry schema, ramp templates; customer to upload scripts and traffic slice; plan baseline week then streaming acceptance. Thanks all.
[61:45] Jordan: Thanks team.
[61:50] Priya: Thanks.

--- End transcript ---
